result:
The answer below is recalled from the known solution of this problem, not derived in full. I only checked the easy upper bound m ≤ 35 myself.

Give each red cell the pair (row count, column count) of its row and column. The first condition says these pairs are all distinct.

The two rows with m red cells each contain 2m red cells. Each of these cells has row count m, so their column counts must be 2m distinct values. That needs at least 2m distinct columns, so 2m ≤ 70 and m ≤ 35.

The columns with those distinct counts must also be consistent with the red cells they contain, and this tightens the bound. As I recall, the full counting argument gives m = 32, and a construction achieving it exists.

ANSWER: 32
